chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Mahbub from Hammad from Ziyad ibn Sulayman from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who said to his wife after he had entered with her: 'I did not find you a virgin.' He said: 'There is no hadd (fixed punishment) upon him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling when a husband claims his wife was not a virgin after marriage?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a husband's claim of non-virginity after consummation does not incur the hadd of qadhf (fixed punishment for false accusation) against him, distinguishing it from general slander cases. This ruling highlights the specific legal nuance in Shia jurisprudence where the husband's assertion is treated as a matter of marital right and verification rather than a penal offense, often resolved through the wife's testimony or oaths. It underscores the practical application of evidence in family law, prioritizing the resolution of the marital bond over punitive measures in this specific scenario.
